observations: body L1-L4: each formula stands where it is printed, «Qua re» and the label «(α)» at the margin. NL is the side of the right triangle FLN of p. 255: NL² = FN² − FL², with FN = FA = AE − FE = 60ᵖ − ε = 49ᵖ 41′, al-Battānī's radius of the eccentric (p. 78, L36-L37, its square 2468ᵖ 26′); the bars after «AE» and «60ᵖ» (L2) are minus signs.

body L4: formula (α) is wrong in the sign of its last term. Since FEL = 180° − 2 (☾ − ⊙) (p. 255, L37-L38), EL = ε cos FEL/R = −ε cos 2 (☾ − ⊙)/R, not ε cos 2 (☾ − ⊙)/R as on p. 255, L40, and the distance is NE = √((60ᵖ − ε)² − (ε sin 2 (☾ − ⊙)/R)²) + ε cos 2 (☾ − ⊙)/R. This gives 60ᵖ at the syzygies, where the centre of the epicycle is in the apogee A, and 60ᵖ − 2ε = 39ᵖ 22′ at the quadratures, in the perigee; formula (α) as printed gives the reverse, 39ᵖ 22′ at the syzygies and 60ᵖ at the quadratures, and for the double elongation of 135.5° drawn on p. 255, 56ᵖ 31′ instead of 41ᵖ 48′. Al-Battānī's rule (p. 79, L1-L5) adds the product of the cosine below 90° and subtracts it above, and is right. Kept as printed.
body L3: specks at the left of the line and after the formula are not transcribed; the formula ends without a stop.

body L5-L6: the dash after «g)» measures 10.2 pt; heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition, the dash before his name 10.4 pt. P. 79, L7 is «de singulis gradibus residui minutum detrahe»; the note referred to is the end of note d) on p. 254, L12-L18.

body L7-L10: the dash after «h)» measures 9.8 pt, the hyphen of «9-12» 3.6 pt. P. 79, L9-L12 puts the eccentricity of the Sun, 2ᵖ 4′ ¾, for the 5ᵖ ¼ of the epicycle of the Moon; 60ᵖ sin 1° 59′ 10″ (al-Battānī's greatest equation of the Sun) is 2ᵖ 4′ 46″.

body L11-L18: «cap. XXX, p. 61» gives the least, mean and greatest distances of the Sun, 1070, 1108 and 1146 radii of the Earth. 1108 : 60 = 18ᵖ 28′ 0″ and (1108 + 1146) : 2 = 1127, 1127 : 60 = 18ᵖ 47′ 0″, as printed. «al–Battānī» (L14) has a long dash (5.4 pt).

body L19-L21: the numbers in Arabic letters are لح (30 + 8 = 38) of the codex, ىح or يح (10 + 8 = 18), whose tooth was taken for a lām, مو (46) and مز (47); ىح is printed without dots, يح with the two dots of the yā' joined into one inside the bowl of the ḥā'. The 47′ is printed مر, without the dot of the zāy; kept as printed. The 38ᵖ 46′ 24″ are p. 79, L11.
body L22-L23: the dash after «i)» measures 9.5 pt, the hyphen of «34-39» 3.6 pt.

body L24-L32: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the meridian ABGD (radius 55.4 pt), the horizon from B through E and T to D, the vertical circle from the zenith A through H and E to G and the ecliptic from Z through H and T to the meridian, as arcs of circles fitted to the print (radius 266.4, 269.3 and 256.8 pt), and the bold italic letters where they are printed. «130–31» (L29) has a long dash (5.4 pt); the bar after «90°» (L27) is a minus sign.

body L30-L34: L30 is the theorem of Menelaus for the triangle AZH cut by the horizon, which meets AZ produced in B, AH produced in E and ZH produced in T. With BA = EA = 90°, so that chord 2BA = chord 2EA = 2R, ZB the altitude of the culminating degree, ZT and TH its distance and that of the Moon from the ascendant and HE = h, it gives L32 and the rule (α), which is al-Battānī's of p. 79, L34-L38: the sine of the distance of the Moon from the ascendant times R, divided by the sine of the distance of the culminating degree from the ascendant, times the sine of the altitude of the culminating degree, divided by R.
